resources.string:
Effective date: October 7, 2026.

Chronicle is a Baylor College of Medicine research data-collection app for one approved study enrollment per installation. Before collection begins, the app identifies the study and its HTTPS server, shows the requested data types, and records consent choices.

This release may collect app package names and labels, app foreground/background and timing events, including each event Android keeps in the same usage history (Activity Resumed, Activity Paused, Activity Stopped, Screen Interactive, Screen Non-interactive, Keyguard Shown, Keyguard Hidden, Device Startup, Device Shutdown, Configuration Change, User Interaction, Shortcut Invocation, Foreground Service Start, Foreground Service Stop, Notification Seen, Notification Interruption and Standby Bucket Changed, and any other event type by its number; which app and when, never notification text), an optional in-app activity-class name, device lifecycle events, battery and charging state, connectivity state, selected device settings, upload-delivery diagnostics, and whether the device user selects study participant or someone else after unlock. Enrollment also sends the device model, manufacturer, and Android version. Research records are encrypted on the device and uploaded over authenticated HTTPS only to the enrolled study server.

When an upload fails, Chronicle keeps a diagnostic record of that occurrence containing the affected upload family, closed failure category, count and time, HTTP status when available, and bounded exception class. After connectivity recovers, it is sent under the active participant/device enrollment and retained through the study's data-retention period unless the participant or study is explicitly erased. The diagnostic record contains no server URL, free-form error text, invitation secret, API key, authorization token, password, or stack trace.

This release does not collect Health Connect or other health records, activity or sleep recognition, continuous hardware-sensor measurements, audio or media metadata, notification content or Notification Activity module records, accessibility interactions, physical location, contacts, messages, typed text, websites, searches, screenshots, photos, videos, microphone recordings, advertising identifiers, financial information, or advertising profiles. It contains no advertising or cross-app tracking SDK.

Use Withdraw from study in Chronicle Settings to stop collection and send a withdrawal request to the enrolled study server. Withdrawing stops collection at once. Data already collected is kept or erased by the study team, according to this study's withdrawal policy. Keep the app installed and connected until the request is acknowledged. Uninstalling also stops future collection and Android removes Chronicle's on-device app data, but an uninstall cannot notify the enrolled study server. Questions about participation or records already uploaded must go to the research team identified in the study consent.

Children and study eligibility. Chronicle is not a general consumer service for children. A minor may participate only under an approved study protocol with any required parent or guardian permission and participant assent.

Baylor College of Medicine general institutional privacy policy is available at https://www.bcm.edu/privacy. Application support: uzairalam998@gmail.com.

Upload delivery diagnostics. Chronicle reports upload success, failure, retry, collection-access loss, app crash, native crash and app not responding diagnostics as separate records, each with its count and occurrence time, including HTTP status and bounded exception class where available; the phone groups them by day in its recent daily history. These diagnostics exclude research content, participant labels, credentials, server URLs, free-form error text, and stack traces. Diagnostics follow study retention and explicit enrollment erasure.
